reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A recurrent deletion of roughly 600 kb generated by non-allelic homologous recombination between the flanking segmental duplications (breakpoints BP4-BP5)
One of the commonest single-locus causes of autism spectrum disorder, developmental delay and speech/language impairment
Deletion carriers tend towards obesity and a larger head circumference (macrocephaly)
The reciprocal duplication of the same interval typically has mirror-image effects, being linked to low body weight and microcephaly
Epilepsy, motor coordination difficulty and a characteristic articulation disorder are frequently seen
Expressivity is highly variable and penetrance incomplete, so the change is often inherited from a mildly affected or unaffected parent
Psychiatric and behavioural features vary widely and may not emerge until later childhood or adolescence
Chromosomal microarray is the first-line diagnostic investigation
reference.pathophysiology: The proximal 16p11.2 region is bounded by segmental duplications that mediate non-allelic homologous recombination, producing a recurrent deletion or its reciprocal duplication. The interval contains around two dozen dosage-sensitive genes important for synaptic function, brain growth and energy balance. Loss of one copy disturbs neurodevelopmental and appetite-regulating pathways, predisposing to autism, language delay and macrocephaly, and shifting weight regulation towards obesity. The reciprocal gain frequently produces opposite effects such as underweight and microcephaly, illustrating the dosage sensitivity of the region. A second genetic hit and background modifier genes probably contribute to the wide variability between individuals.
additionalDifferentials: Prader-Willi syndrome and other syndromic obesity in a carrier presenting with weight gain
Monogenic obesity such as MC4R-related obesity
additionalInvestigations: Chromosomal microarray as first-line to detect and size the copy-number change
FISH or MLPA to confirm the deletion
Parental studies to establish inheritance and counsel recurrence risk
EEG if a seizure disorder is suspected
redFlags: Rapid weight gain with emerging complications of obesity
Marked feeding or swallowing difficulty in infancy
reference.prognosis: The neurodevelopmental outlook ranges from mild learning and speech difficulties to more significant intellectual disability and autism; early intervention improves functional outcomes. Metabolic complications of obesity are an important long-term concern in deletion carriers, so weight surveillance materially influences overall health.
pitfalls: Dismissing an inherited deletion as benign despite the well-recognised variable expressivity
Attributing all of a child's difficulties to the deletion and missing coexisting or treatable conditions
Neglecting weight and metabolic surveillance in deletion carriers
Failing to distinguish the deletion from the reciprocal duplication, which carries a different weight and head-size profile
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Provide early developmental intervention with speech-and-language therapy, behavioural support for autism spectrum features and individualised educational support
Control epilepsy with appropriate antiseizure medication where seizures occur
Monitor growth and body-mass index in deletion carriers, with active obesity prevention through dietary and activity measures
Offer occupational therapy and physiotherapy for motor coordination difficulty and targeted therapy for the articulation disorder
Undertake formal autism and cognitive assessment to direct support
Provide genetic counselling with parental testing and recurrence-risk advice, recognising variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance
Coordinate care through a developmental paediatrics multidisciplinary team
